{% raw %}
The DC Dark Legion module adds Gotham and Krypton Rush seasons and Red Boxes, the train and Guardian rotations, team assignments and the battle tracker. Finish [**Setting up Alagos**](/guides/setting-up/) first.

## 1. Switch it on

Run `/guild-settings modules` and press **Switch on**. Its commands appear within a few seconds, and its jobs show up in `/guild-settings permissions`, where you can share them with other roles (for example, who may run the train).

Switching it off later hides everything it added and stops its scheduled runs. Nothing is deleted: switching it back on brings it all back. A game you switch off can be switched on again after 7 days, so switch off only when you mean to. Switched it off by mistake? Switch it back on within 10 minutes and nothing is lost.

## 2. Its channels

In `/guild-settings show`, open the **DC Dark Legion** tab and press **✏️ Edit channels** for:

- **Train Post**: where the daily train is posted.
- **Guardian Post**: where the weekly Guardian rotation is posted.
- **Battle Tracker**: where the City Hall tracker panel is posted when a Gotham match starts.
- **Battle Call-outs** (optional): one line per capture, for relaying in game; without it they go to the Battle Tracker channel.

`/train-run` and `/guardian-run` refuse until their channel is set, and say so. A Guardian run also needs at least one city (section 4).

## 3. Your roster's game details

Each player's power and rank live on the roster. Officers set them in `/roster` (open a player, or use **Bulk power** for many at once). Players set their own train seat preferences and the events they can make in `/my-profile` once they have claimed their character.

## 4. Guardian cities

On the same **DC Dark Legion** tab press **🏙️ Guardian cities**, then **➕ Add city** for each city you defend. Give its name and its city guardian (a name on your roster). Up to 25 cities.

Each city works one of two ways:

- **Static**: the city keeps one fixed city guardian, and each week's rotation fills its Banker, Architect and Researcher posts from your eligible players.
- **Rotation**: a named group of players covers the whole city and takes turns at all four posts. Press **Switch to rotation**, then **➕ Add members**. **Guardian minimum** can require a rank or a power for the guardian post; if nobody in the group qualifies that week, last week's guardian keeps it. A player can be in one city's group only.

A city you no longer use can be **retired**: it leaves the rotation but keeps its history. **Delete** is only offered for a city that has never been used.

### Who the rotations may pick

On the same tab, **🚂 Train eligibility** and **🛡️ Guardian eligibility** show the rules in plain words. Pick a preset from the menu:

- **Standard** (the default): the last 7 days of Guardian, Krypton Rush, Gotham and Forge Breach for the train, with the top 15 by power as Conductors (two attendances needed); Guardian first and Gotham if needed for the Guardian rotation, with Officer/R4 left out.
- **Relaxed**: 14 days back, and one attendance is enough to be Conductor. For smaller or less active leagues.
- **Any activity**: every event counts, your own event types included.

On a paid plan, **✏️ Customise** sets each value yourself: days to look back, which event types count, attendances needed, the size of the Conductor tier and how many of it are picked first, and ranks to leave out. Changes apply from the next run, reroll or reset; a run already posted is not changed. City guardians, this cycle's Conductors and "already served this cycle" are not settings: they are what keeps the rotation fair.

## 5. Automatic runs (Premium)

On **Premium**, the train and Guardian rotation can run by themselves. On **Free**, run them by hand with `/train-run` and `/guardian-run` (or **Run train** and **Run Guardian** on the officer panel): everything else about them is the same.

Run `/schedule` to see the runs this server has set up, and press **➕ New schedule** to have the train or the Guardian rotation run by itself:

- choose **Train** or **Guardian**, and how often (usually daily for the train, weekly for Guardian);
- **Set time** (your server's time) and, for weekly, **Set day**;
- press **Confirm**. It warns you if the post channel is not set yet.

`/schedule` also changes a run's time or switches it off (pick it from the menu), and warns you if one is set up twice or cannot post. If your server moves to Free, its schedules are kept but do not run; switching one off still works.

**The first runs on a new server may come out empty**: players qualify with confirmed attendance at certain events in the last week (🚂 Train eligibility and 🛡️ Guardian eligibility on the DC Dark Legion tab). Record attendance with Finish & Save for a week, or choose a broader preset.

The train posts to the Train Post channel and the Guardian rotation to the Guardian Post channel. A scheduled run is skipped on a day an officer has already run it by hand. You can always run them yourself with `/train-run` and `/guardian-run`.

## 6. Gotham and team posts

For Gotham events, create the event as normal and set its type to **Gotham Events** in the editor. Its **Notifications** tab then has a **Team Post** time: the team assignments are posted automatically at that time each week. Set the standing teams the post uses with `/teams show` → **✏️ Assign players** (any plan). On Premium, `/teams setup` can build them for you and `/teams composition` sets how many players each team gets and how they are picked. See [**Team assignments**](/guides/teams/).

Seasons start themselves: confirming attendance on a Battle for Gotham opens a new Gotham season. Krypton Rush seasons are counted in 4-week blocks from your first season; `/akr-season set-start` sets that start if it needs correcting.
